newsitem.title: UK: Abbey rebuff raises NatWest questions.
newsitem.headline: Abbey rebuff raises NatWest questions.

text.p: British bank shares were mixed on Tuesday as the market realised a rumoured 25 billion pound ($41 billion) merger between Abbey National and National Westminster will not happen though analysts see logic in such a deal.

NatWest shares, which had risen 80p in the past two sessions on talk of a bid or merger, went into reverse on Tuesday, shedding 19p to 797p as sellers took profits. Abbey National gained 6.5p to 890p.
The failure of NatWest's approach has led to questions being asked again about the bank's strategy which it had hoped it had clarified over the past couple of years.
Recently, analysts have been more worried about the performance of NatWest's two main divisions, NatWest UK, the branch banking business, and NatWest Markets, the investment banking arm.
"The problem is that NatWest UK isn't as profitable as other banks' operations," said one analyst, "and the returns from NatWest Markets are also lower than target."
NatWest is trying to cut costs in branch banking but is spending a lot of money trying to establish Markets as a "global" investment banking force.
Now that NatWest seems to have admitted that it is dissatisfied with its previous strategy, many analysts feel its only alternative is to plough on with trying to improve returns from the business.
"It may well be that they (NatWest) have taken a look at the retail market and felt they had to do something about it," said another analyst.
The purchase of Abbey National would have added the country's second largest mortgage lender, a high degree of retail expertise, excellent brand name and a tie-in to supermarket banking with Safeway.
But analysts say the Abbey is likely to have been worried that it would be swamped by NatWest and is also unlikely to have been over-enthusiastic about NatWest Markets.

Abbey chief executive Peter Birch is known to favour further strategic acquisitions but will not over pay just to get a deal done. He recently said in an interview with Reuters that Abbey wants to be counter-cyclical in its strategic moves.
Birch is reported to have spoken in favour of merging with NatWest but newspaper reports that he wants to do one more big deal before he retires next year wre dismissed by analysts.
"The Abbey is opportunistic," said one analyst, "but it won't do deals just for the sake of it."($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
